issue: An early upright dive overlap could disappear during tipping before the later robust contact window, although the native client could already have sent its first claim.
changes: First-touch sampling includes both sides of the analytic upright-to-tipped capsule boundary and adapts for DB dives.
A bounded 6ms/128-sample scan requires the first overlap to connect to the selected contact window. Nominal, dispatch-delay variants, and fresh jump/dive validation retain this check.
DB connection scans run only when a candidate can improve the existing action score. Opponent possible-reach predictions remain optimistic.
performanceScope: Single offline runs of the connection change before the separately validated DB continuous-jump integration. Concurrent host workloads affect timing. These are not Roblox frame-time measurements or a guarantee of a sub200ms live solve.
limitations: Contact/ball positions are predictions from logged throw data; server-side rejection reasons are not available.
Some successful native catches also had disconnected nominal windows, so the gap is a robustness defect, not proof that it caused every failure.
A sampled connection check is not a mathematical continuous-collision or network guarantee.
No native extracted source, player identities, or credentials included.
